title: Composition of H-projective morphisms
statement: If $g:X\to Y$ and $h:Y\to S$ are H-projective morphisms [def-kun-projective], then the composite $h\circ g:X\to S$ is H-projective.

proof.text: By the definition of H-projectivity [def-kun-projective], choose integers $n,m\geq0$ and closed immersions $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ over $Y$ and $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_S$ over $S$. Thus $g=\pi_Y\circ i$ and $h=\pi_S\circ j$, with $\pi_Y:\mathbf P^n_Y\to Y$ and $\pi_S:\mathbf P^m_S\to S$ the structural projections.

Put $Q=\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf P^m_S}$. Apply [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] with coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ to $j:Y\to\mathbf P^m_S$. It identifies $\mathbf P^n_Y$ with $Y\times_{\mathbf P^m_S}Q$ and its map $q:\mathbf P^n_Y\to Q$ with the base change of $j$ along the structural projection $Q\to\mathbf P^m_S$. Since $j$ is a closed immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $q$ a closed immersion. The cartesian square gives $\pi_Q\circ q=j\circ\pi_Y$, where $\pi_Q:Q\to\mathbf P^m_S$.

Apply [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] again, this time to $\pi_S:\mathbf P^m_S\to S$ with the same coordinate set. This identifies $Q$ over $\mathbf P^m_S$ with $\mathbf P^m_S\times_S\mathbf P^n_S$. Swapping the two projections gives $Q\cong\mathbf P^n_S\times_S\mathbf P^m_S$: the swap and its inverse are the maps specified by the reversed pairs of projections, and both composites are identities by the fibre-product universal property. Under this cartesian identification $q\circ i$ is a closed immersion $k:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S\times_S\mathbf P^m_S$, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] applied to $i$ and $q$. Its composite with the second projection is $j\circ g$, by the square in step 2, and hence its structure morphism to $S$ is $h\circ g$.

By [lem-chow-segre], compose $k$ with the Segre closed immersion $s:\mathbf P^n_S\times_S\mathbf P^m_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{nm+n+m}_S$. The same cited statement says that this composite of a closed immersion into the product with $s$ is a closed immersion. Both maps are over $S$, so for $e=s\circ k$ and the structural projection $\pi:\mathbf P^{nm+n+m}_S\to S$ one has $\pi\circ e=h\circ g$. The integer $nm+n+m$ is nonnegative. This is precisely a finite projective-space closed-immersion factorization as required by [def-kun-projective], proving H-projectivity of $h\circ g$.
